Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Public Prosecutor for t  respondent/State.
Heard on I.A. No.19112/2025, which is second application under Section 430(1) of BNSS/389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant-Manish Lodhi, S/o Dhan Prasad Lodhi.

The appellant is aggrieved of the judgment dated 03/08/2021 passed by the learned Special Judge,
POCSO Act, Sagar (MP) in Special Case No.14/2019, whereby the appellant-Manish Lodhi stands convicted and sentenced as under :-
 Conviction Sentence  
 Section Act Imprisonment Fine  
 366A R.I. for IPC Rs.500/- 
 10 years  376(AB)
 of IPC Life  read with Imprisonment S.5(m)/6 I.P.C./POCSO (as per Section  Rs.500/- 
 of Act 53 of IPC till  POCSO natural life of  Act appellant)
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that present is a case of false 2 CRA-5664-2021 implication.

It is submitted that all prosecutions' witnesses namely victim herself and her parents Manish Lodhi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148786194/
1 have turned hostile.

sentences.text: They have not supported prosecution case.
There was a dispute between accused-Manish Lodhi and the family members of the victim on account of raising of a wall.
It is also submitted that there was an illicit relationship between some members of the families which became bone of contention for which appellant-Manish Lodhi has been falsely implicated.
It is further submitted that appellant is in custody since last four years.
Hence, prayer is made to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail.

Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Public Prosecutor, in his turn, submits that Dr. Akanksha Jain (PW-3) who had examined the victim clearly deposed that tampering with hymen was observed by the doctor because there was swelling and redness around the private part.
It is also submitted that Ex.P/31 is the DNA report which is positive, hence, prayer is made to dismissed the application for suspension of sentence.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Ossification test report (Ex.P/10) of the victim reveals that her age was certified by the doctor to be between 13 to 14 years.
Ex.P/31 is the DNA report which reveals that DNA qua underwear and vaginal swab of the victim matched with the blood samples of the accused namely Manish Lodhi.

When this fact is taken into consideration, then even if the witnesses have turned hostile, but looking to the age of the victim as has come in the ossification test report, victim cannot be accepted to be a consenting party.

She was a child in terms of the definition of a 'child' given under POCSO Act,
2012.

When these facts are taken into consideration and though we are not sure as to under what context victim and her family members turned hostile, but, scientific evidence corroborates the fact that victim privacy was violated, therefore, we refuse to show indulgence.
Accordingly, I.A. No.19112/2025 is dismissed.
